idiom_name: two-pass decode: kind field + json.RawMessage, then Unmarshal into the concrete struct
implementation_notes: Go has no inheritance and no runtime type metadata for JSON, so the local idiom is an envelope struct with a kind field plus json.RawMessage: decode the envelope, switch on the kind, then unmarshal the raw bytes into the concrete struct - encoding/json only allocates the target type named in the second pass, which is exactly the identify-then-parse split the pattern asks for. For generated protobuf messages the same job is done by anypb.UnmarshalNew, which resolves the type_url against the compiled-in registry. The GoF-style factory with an interface per message is rarely needed: a map from tag to decoder function replaces it and is the form to use when new types must plug in without editing the switch.
pitfalls: encoding/json matches keys case-insensitively, so Kind, kind and KIND all populate the same field and a payload can smuggle a tag the producer never wrote; never rely on case to distinguish tags.

Decoding a polymorphic field into interface{} yields map[string]any with every number as float64, so large integer ids silently lose precision - always unmarshal from json.RawMessage into a concrete struct.
Registration through init() in another package is only linked when that package is imported (use a blank import), so a forgotten import surfaces as an unknown-kind error at runtime.
